findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the Bedrock InvokeModel alarm criterion (and the terraform Scope bullet) to require the alarm publish to the review bot's existing SNS topic — `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` (and ok_actions), matching the parent 061c AC and the gate-critical WS7/1fa8/88ab wiring — so 'forced test notification' is delivered via SNS rather than only asserted.
evidence: Parent 061c AC: '…a CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate — threshold >25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods — publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic.'

Leaf alarm AC enumerates 'a metric_query metric-math expression … dimensioned by ModelId … thresholds … present as literal values … METRIC SOURCE comment' and a separate ARN/forced-notification AC, but never names alarm_actions or the SNS topic.

aws_sns_topic.alerts = 'rebar-gerrit-alerts' exists (infra/terraform/monitoring.tf:36) with an email subscription; gate-critical alarms wire it via alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn] (monitoring_ws7.tf:52, monitoring_1fa8.tf:74, monitoring_88ab.tf:62).

infra/terraform/monitoring_88ab.tf:30-32: 'an alarm without an action fires silently' — the exact failure mode a metric-only Bedrock alarm would exhibit; the S4b voter_errors alarm is deliberately metric-only, so 'declare a Bedrock alarm' does not by itself satisfy the SNS-publish clause.
S9 source-material (eb6e comment Part 4 §6.5 item 26) independently flags the same SNS/ARN gap: the existing eb6e alarm has 'NO ARN … and NO forced test notification recorded.'
findings.finding: The leaf's Bedrock InvokeModel alarm criterion omits the parent AC's explicit requirement that the alarm 'publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic' — it specifies metric source, dimensioning, thresholds, state, and ARN + forced-notification recording, but never requires the SNS action wiring the parent mandates.
findings.location: Scope > infra/terraform/ bullet and AC 'a Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm is declared…'; parent 061c final AC ('publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic')
scenarios: Bedrock partially degrades (>25% client-error rate) post-cutover; the alarm transitions to ALARM but, lacking alarm_actions, no operator is paged, so a degraded no-fallback gate runs unnoticed — the exact partial-degradation case the leaf says voter_errors cannot catch.

An implementer satisfies the leaf's alarm AC (metric-math + thresholds + a state datapoint) with a metric-only alarm and produces a 'forced test notification' via set-alarm-state or a manual publish, leaving the parent's SNS-publish requirement unmet.
findings.suggested_fix: In the alarm AC add: 'and wires alarm_actions (and ok_actions) to aws_sns_topic.alerts (infra/terraform/monitoring.tf), mirroring the gate-critical WS7/1fa8/88ab alarms, so a partially-degraded Bedrock pages the operator — the S4b voter_errors metric-only pattern is NOT sufficient here.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm's notification wiring: set alarm_actions (and ok_actions) to the shared aws_sns_topic.alerts, following the gate-critical-alarm convention in monitoring_ws7.tf/monitoring_1fa8.tf rather than the dashboard-only S4b/S5 pattern, so the 'forced test notification' AC is producible.
evidence: Plan Scope names 'a Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm ... metric_query ... thresholds ... with the alarm ARN and a forced test notification recorded' but never mentions alarm_actions/ok_actions or aws_sns_topic.alerts.
monitoring_ws7.tf:21-22 'Unlike the S5/S4b alarms, this one WIRES SNS (a774 requires an actual alert): a sustained mirror divergence pages the operator.' with alarm_actions/ok_actions at :52-53.

monitoring_1fa8.tf:72-75 'WIRE SNS (unlike S5/S4b): a broken CI dispatcher blocks all submits once the gate is active, so page the operator' — the same gate-critical rationale that applies to a Bedrock alarm guarding the LLM-Review vote.
monitoring_s4b.tf and monitoring_s5.tf declare NO alarm_actions, so a Bedrock alarm modeled on them would be dashboard-only and could not emit the forced test notification the AC requires.
findings.finding: The plan's new Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm specifies its metric source, metric-math, dimensioning and thresholds but never specifies its NOTIFICATION target (alarm_actions/ok_actions to the shared aws_sns_topic.alerts). Its own acceptance criterion requires 'one FORCED test notification recorded', which is not producible from an alarm that has no alarm_actions. The repo's convention is explicit: gate-critical alarms wire SNS (monitoring_ws7.tf:52-53, monitoring_1fa8.tf:74-75), while the S4b/S5 host-metric alarms deliberately do not — so the correct choice is not obvious and must be stated.
findings.location: Scope → infra/terraform/ (the Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm); AC 'the alarm's ARN and one FORCED test notification are recorded'
scenarios: Bedrock partially degrades (still votes) so voter_errors stays OK; the Bedrock client-error alarm transitions to ALARM but, lacking alarm_actions, notifies no one and the degradation runs unobserved.
Implementer builds the alarm exactly per the stated Scope, then cannot satisfy the 'forced test notification' AC because no SNS action is wired.

findings.finding: The plan does not specify the new alarm's missing-data treatment. For an error-RATE alarm, a fully-down Bedrock emitting no invocation datapoints (rate undefined / no data) can sit in INSUFFICIENT_DATA and never breach if the repo's default `treat_missing_data = notBreaching` is inherited — leaving the total-outage case uncovered.
findings.location: Scope → 'infra/terraform/ — a Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm'
findings.suggested_fix: Either choose `treat_missing_data` explicitly for the rate metric with a rationale, or pair the rate alarm with a low-`Invocations`/no-data companion alarm so a fully-down Bedrock (zero invocations) still surfaces.

findings.finding: The new Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm is specified by thresholds only; its METRIC SOURCE and the computation of the 'client-error rate > 25% of invocations' are unspecified — unlike every other custom alarm in this repo, which documents its metric source and (for host-published metrics) the dimensionless publish/alarm contract.
findings.location: Scope → 'infra/terraform/ — a Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm'; AC 'a Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm is declared in infra/terraform/'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope/AC that the alarm uses `metric_query` metric-math over the AWS/Bedrock `Invocations` and client-error metrics (dimensioned by the invoked model/inference profile) to compute a 25% error-rate threshold; if instead a custom `rebar/host` metric is chosen, document the dimensionless publish/alarm contract as the other two alarms do and add the publisher to observability.sh (noting that would re-open the 'observability.sh not in scope' claim).

ORDERING AC requires the alarm to land 'in a commit that precedes the compose flip', while the datapoint AC requires 'real Bedrock traffic'
findings.finding: The AC requiring the Bedrock client-error alarm to be observed in OK/ALARM (not INSUFFICIENT_DATA) with a datapoint 'after real Bedrock traffic' may be unsatisfiable pre-cutover for the opus (frontier) and haiku (trivial) ModelId dimensions, because the plan only cites us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 as having prior epic traffic, and the review bot does not itself invoke Bedrock until AFTER the compose flip — yet the ordering AC requires the alarm to land and be proven BEFORE the flip.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'the alarm is proven to be watching something that EXISTS'; and ORDERING AC (alarm lands first); Scope — Bedrock alarm 'dimensioned by ModelId'
scenarios: Alarm declared per-ModelId dimensioned on the opus profile that has no pre-cutover invocations, so its state reads INSUFFICIENT_DATA, failing the 'not INSUFFICIENT_DATA' AC before the flip that would generate its traffic
findings.suggested_fix: Either dimension the alarm on the sonnet ModelId that already has traffic (and note the frontier/opus coverage is proven post-cutover via the happy-path run), or explicitly move the datapoint-existence check to a post-cutover verification with the ordering AC requiring only the alarm's declaration + forced-test-notification pre-flip.
